findings.title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars query, so stale cache status stays on screen
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop (which maps to `onChanged` in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` and is undefined in most call sites). Unlike `disconnectMutation`, it does not call `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`. After the user confirms deletion, the dropdown continues to show the old 'Last updated' timestamp and the 'Delete cached data' item until a full reload, making it look like the deletion failed. Add an `onSettled`/`onSuccess` that invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`.

findings.title: Throws plain Error instead of TRPCError, surfacing as 500
findings.body: When the credential does not belong to the user (or does not exist) the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps non-TRPCError exceptions to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, so an authorization failure is reported to clients (and to Sentry) as a server crash rather than a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN response. Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or FORBIDDEN) consistent with other handlers in this router.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId, breaking existing callers
findings.body: The `UserWithCalendars` type (exported and re-used by platform libraries) was tightened so that `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` must include `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. Any caller that builds this object from a narrower Prisma select (only `externalId`, `integration`, `eventTypeId`) will now fail type-checking, and nothing in `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` actually reads these new fields. Only `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated in this PR. Either revert the type change (the fields are unused) or update all producers, including `@calcom/platform-libraries` consumers.

findings.title: Unused bulk write to SelectedCalendar on every webhook/cache refresh
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now runs `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` after every cache refresh, i.e. on every Google webhook notification. It touches every SelectedCalendar row for the credential (including calendars not involved in the refresh and event-type-level rows) solely to bump `updatedAt`, but nothing in the frontend consumes `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` — the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`. This is an extra write per webhook with no consumer, and it overloads the semantics of `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. The PR description itself questions whether it should be removed; it should.

findings.title: Cache timestamp hard-coded to en-US locale
findings.body: The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, ignoring the user's locale, time format preference and timezone (`useLocale` already exposes the locale). Non-US users will see a US-style date/time in an otherwise localized UI.

findings.title: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only; script fails on Linux
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is the macOS syntax for in-place editing. GNU sed interprets `''` as the input filename and errors out, so the GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL update fails on Linux developer machines. Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory rather than the script location, so running it from the repo root creates a stray `.env` one directory up. Use a portable approach (e.g. a temp file + mv, or detect sed flavor) and derive the path from `$(dirname "$0")`.

findings.title: dev:cron uses npx tsx but tsx is not a declared dependency
findings.body: The script was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, yet `tsx` is not listed in dependencies or devDependencies (ts-node still is). `npx` will attempt a network download of the latest `tsx` at run time, which is non-reproducible and fails offline/in locked-down CI. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency or keep `ts-node`.

findings.title: No tests for new deleteCache handler or getCacheStatusByCredentialIds
findings.body: The PR adds a new authenticated mutation that deletes user data, a new repository aggregation (`groupBy` on `credentialId` with `_max.updatedAt`) and a modified `connectedCalendarsHandler` that merges cache status into the response, but adds no unit or integration tests. In particular, the ownership check (another user's credentialId must be rejected) and the credentialId→cacheUpdatedAt mapping are untested. The PR description also states end-to-end testing was not possible locally.
